facts.text: I want you to interview me about what I'm interested in my life.
I think many people don't have a sense of purpose but can still be happy.
I think people may take purpose too seriously and get pressured because they don't have clear goals or a sense of purpose.
I agree that purpose matters, but I'm not sure how to achieve a balance.
I ask whether different approaches can include living without a sense of purpose at all.
I want you to ask me one open question at a time and then ask the next question based on my answer.
I sometimes choose doing something randomly, like picking and reading a random book.
Picking ideas randomly helps me keep myself open to ideas I never thought about.
I talk with friends about the purpose of life and how to define goals.
I can get ideas from other people by listening to their views and ideas and how they maintain their balance.
I think a sense of purpose is limited in time and I feel it from time to time.
I think goals are overrated and can lead to frustration.
I think society is too much goal oriented.
I think goal-oriented culture is rooted in our culture and causes frustration for many people instead of helping create a balanced life experience.
I think goals are usually related to results rather than the process.
I think if a goal is an outcome, an individual may focus only on how to get that specific goal while ignoring other opportunities and optional outcomes.
I think if the process is the main focus, one may decide to focus on certain processes and enjoy the process rather than the outcome.
I use the example of taking care of a cactus without the goal of making it big, just for the sake of taking care of it.
I ask for more relevant examples from day-to-day life.
